name: Stepping stone
description: A flat stone set into the ground, inviting a slower path through the garden.

name: Stone path
description: Fitted paving stones that join one part of the garden to another.

name: Stone arrangement
description: A small, asymmetrical grouping of stones. Its gaps make cool hiding places.

facts.text: Odd-numbered, uneven groupings are traditional in Japanese stone arrangement.

name: Stone lantern
description: A weathered stone lantern, half-hidden by moss. It has watched over the garden for a long time.

name: Old boulder
description: A large, lichen-spotted boulder, settled deep into the ground.

name: Old garden gate
description: A wooden gate in the garden wall. Beyond it lies the next garden of the sanctuary.

name: Stone basin
description: A low stone water basin, the kind visitors once knelt at to rinse their hands. It still catches the rain.

facts.text: Low basins like this are called tsukubai, from a word meaning to crouch.

name: Bamboo fence
description: A low fence of bound canes that frames a planting and gives small creatures cover.

facts.text: Low bamboo fences like this traditionally edge paths and planting beds.

name: Bamboo water spout
description: A bamboo pipe that trickles water into a stone basin, with a gentle, rhythmic sound.

facts.text: Moving water brings birds down to drink and bathe.

name: Maple-leaf lantern
description: A small stone lantern dressed with red maple leaves, glowing softly at dusk.

name: Standing stone
description: A tall, weathered stone set upright in the gravel.

facts.text: Lichen grows slowly on bare stone, a few millimetres a year.

name: Raked gravel
description: Gravel raked into gentle ripples, like water.

facts.text: The ripples are raked afresh after rain.

name: Fallen log
description: An old trunk, soft with moss, slowly returning to the soil.

facts.text: Fungi slowly break the wood down into soil.

name: Log stack
description: A loose stack of deadwood, left to rot for wildlife.

facts.text: Fungi grow beside it once the wood begins to soften.

name: Little cascade
description: A tumble of stones where the stream drops and sings.

facts.text: Moving water carries fresh air into the stream.

name: Resting stone
description: A broad, flat stone set in the stream for birds to stand on.

facts.text: Wagtails stand on stones in the water, bobbing their tails.
